clue.text: A chat with Mrs T, and I cocked up the treaty

indicators.note: something cocked up has been botched, so these letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: Mrs Thatcher's nickname gives the letters MRST

explanation.surface: Thatcher over tea, botching a famous treaty she would later rail against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocked up' rearranges A CHAT, MRS T and I; 'with' and 'and' just join them.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1992 agreement founding the European Union is named after the Dutch city where it was signed.

clue.text: Prices advocated but rarely maintained by politicians

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the worth put on goods

definitions.text: advocated but rarely maintained by politicians

explanation.walkthrough: In 1993-94 John Major's 'Back to Basics' campaign preached traditional moral standards while ministers' scandals piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both monetary worth of things and the moral principles a person professes to hold.

clue.text: Broadcasting watchdog: one who looks up a lot of pussy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: William ... chaired the Broadcasting Standards Council, Britain's TV decency regulator

definitions.text: one who looks up a lot of pussy
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a smut censor, whose job means viewing a great deal of pornography

explanation.walkthrough: Lord Rees-Mogg, former Times editor, ran the Broadcasting Standards Council from 1988, monitoring sex and violence on television.
explanation.definitionFit: As the council's chairman he was the official guardian of taste on British airwaves, a watchdog over broadcasters.

clue.text: Thatcher originated Lamont's downfall — period

indicators.note: the start of the word Thatcher is what is taken, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Thatcher
the Exchange Rate Mechanism, whose collapse on Black Wednesday in 1992 ruined Chancellor Norman Lamont

explanation.surface: Thatcher took Britain into the currency system that later finished off her successor's Chancellor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originated' takes T from Thatcher; ERM is the Exchange Rate Mechanism, which Thatcher joined in 1990; sterling's forced exit in 1992 cost Lamont his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed span of time, such as a school term or a term of office.

clue.text: Religious leaders put up ban on transsexuals

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down clue, put up means the word is written bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: to bar is to ban
bis is slang for bisexuals, loosely used here for people of unconventional sexuality

explanation.surface: Clerics raise a prohibition against transsexual people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns BAR into RAB, and 'on' sets it above BIS. The setter's 'transsexuals' is loose: BIS is slang for bisexuals.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher and spiritual head of a congregation.

clue.text: Old dear substituted duck for Auntie's turkey

indicators.note: the letters are swapped around into different places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An elderly woman serves duck instead of turkey for Christmas dinner at her aunt's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substituted' rearranges OLD DEAR plus O. Auntie is the nickname for the BBC; its 1992 Spanish-set soap Eldorado flopped and was axed within a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is a show that fails badly, and this costly soap opera was the BBC's notorious flop.

clue.text: Dick stands on head to screw

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing on its head turns the word upside down, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: to bonk is to have sex, British slang

explanation.surface: Smutty instruction for an acrobatic sex position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands on head' turns BONK upside down in this down entry; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are vulgar slang for the penis.

clue.text: Strip heartless player who bawled

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Paul Gascoigne, known as Gazza, the England footballer who wept at the 1990 World Cup

explanation.surface: A stripper with no feelings who once cried on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle Z from GAZZA, whose tears at the 1990 World Cup became famous. 'Strip' looks like a verb but names the Gaza Strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaza Strip is the narrow coastal territory on the Mediterranean, so the place is a strip of land.

clue.text: Visually challenging, but not a new classified ads section for our randy readers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: staring someone down, confronting them with the eyes

definitions.text: classified ads section for our randy readers
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as EYE (Private Eye) plus BALLING, slang for having sex, it sounds like a smutty small-ads page

explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a new' admits the second reading is a joke: Private Eye has no such section, but EYE + BALLING would suit lonely-hearts ads for its lustful readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard and provocatively, a confrontational glare.

clue.text: Our niche for crap initiated (and swallowed) by screwed up poseur-nerds

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take the single letter inside them
crumpled or messed up, so the letters of the hyphenated words are jumbled
the word crap is only begun, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of crap

explanation.surface: Private Eye mocks its own column of pretentious waffle, the dross that poseurs feed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screwed up' jumbles POSEURNERDS into PSEUDSORNER; 'initiated' gives C from crap, which the jumble has 'swallowed'. 'for', 'and' and 'by' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseuds Corner is Private Eye's long-running column quoting pretentious writing, the magazine's own spot for drivel.

clue.text: Prattish puffed up character spotted on telly

definitions.text: Prattish puffed up character spotted on telly

parts.words: Prattish puffed up character spotted on telly
parts.note: a cryptic description of the pink, yellow-spotted, inflated idiot on Noel Edmonds's Saturday TV show

explanation.walkthrough: Puffed up and spotted sound like insults about a pompous celebrity, but this character really is inflated and covered in spots. Prattish is apt: the Mr title of a pratt.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1990s BBC character was a bulbous pink costume with yellow spots who blundered about clumsily.

clue.text: We hear journalists bed leftie traditionalist

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the words, so they are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: journalists are the press, and a cot is a bed, together sounding like the politician's name

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip that reporters have slept with a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' says PRESS + COT is spoken. John Prescott was the champion of Old Labour traditions in the early 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescott, the left-leaning union-backed MP, stood for Labour's old working-class values against its modernisers.

clue.text: Floating voter's hidden loot

indicators.note: letters that float drift loose, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the word voter, with 's read as 'is' linking it to the definition

explanation.surface: A swing voter's secret money stash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floating voter' looks like one fixed phrase, but 'Floating' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure trove is a store of valuables found hidden, so the word means a concealed hoard.

clue.text: He purged smear surrounding Lamont initially

indicators.note: the first word goes all round the second piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a smear is a stain

indicators.note: only the beginning of Lamont is wanted, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Lamont

explanation.surface: A political smear campaign closing in on the Chancellor Norman Lamont.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dictator ran the Great Purge of the 1930s, executing and imprisoning rivals by the million.

clue.text: Union tub-thumper in a perverse sort of pattern

indicators.note: contrary and twisted, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: paisley is a swirling teardrop fabric pattern

explanation.surface: A rabble-rousing trade unionist in a strangely kinky design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' turns IN A into IAN. 'Union' suggests a trade union, but means the union of Northern Ireland with Britain, which Ian Paisley defended in fiery speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley was the thundering Ulster Unionist preacher and politician, a classic rabble-rousing orator.

clue.text: Junk food turnaround's a rip-off

indicators.note: a turnaround faces the other way, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Macs are Big Mac burgers, fast food

explanation.surface: Fast food is a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle, a dishonest scheme that cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Strip vice-president — not for easy gain

parts.note: a margin is a strip down the edge of a page
Al Gore, US Vice-President from 1993

explanation.surface: Undress the US number two, which will win nothing easily.
explanation.walkthrough: A marginal seat is one held by a slim majority, a fight to win rather than a walkover.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal constituency is closely contested, so neither side can count on winning it comfortably.

clue.text: Band with fab number — a chance of escape for prisoners?

definitions.text: a chance of escape for prisoners?

parts.note: a band is a musical group
the Beatles were the Fab Four, so their number is four

explanation.surface: A Beatles song offering a prison breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: Group 4 was the security firm running Britain's first private prisons and escort services in 1993, embarrassed by a string of escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The firm guarding inmates lost so many in transit that it became a by-word for an opportunity to flee custody.

clue.text: Oats time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: oats cooked into a breakfast
second meaning: in British slang ... is time served in prison

explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is also the 1970s sitcom set in a prison, and 'doing porridge' means serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the oatmeal dish and British slang for a jail sentence.

clue.text: Some heroin kept from the mouth of pigs

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of heroin and the start of kept

explanation.surface: Drugs withheld from police informers' mouths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from 'heroin kept'. 'Pigs' looks like police slang, but the definition is the noise from real pigs' mouths; 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting sound a pig makes, what comes from its mouth.

clue.text: As agitators do in jail, not in bed

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
someone up is out of bed

explanation.surface: Troublemakers in prison refuse to stay in their bunks.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to provoke trouble or incite unrest, what agitators set out to do.

clue.text: She gives public health leaders Ecstasy-swallowing award

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: first letters of public and health

indicators.note: the award takes the drug's letter inside it

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman hands health chiefs an honour with a drug inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a pronoun standing in for a girl's name: PH from 'leaders', then OEBE, the honour 'swallowing' the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a female name, so the pronoun stands in for any woman so named.

clue.text: Actor buggered on Parisian back street — that's official

indicators.note: in an across clue, the jumbled word comes on after the first piece

parts.note: rue is French for street, and back reverses it

indicators.note: broken or ruined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer roughed up on a Paris side street, confirmed by the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back street' looks like an alley, but it is the French street read in reverse; 'buggered' gives OCRAT, set 'on' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is a bureaucrat working for the European Union's institutions, an official.

clue.text: See 10
Prepare to shag — but not Mellor style?

definitions.text: Prepare to shag — but not Mellor style?

parts.words: Prepare to shag — but not Mellor style?
parts.note: getting undressed for sex, unlike Tory minister David Mellor, reputed to have kept his Chelsea football kit on

explanation.walkthrough: In 1992 the tabloids claimed David Mellor made love to an actress in a Chelsea strip; the joke is that he stripped into a strip rather than off.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip off is to take all one's clothes off, the usual preliminary to sex.

clue.text: Church leader hanging around dancers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Desmond ..., Anglican Archbishop of Cape Town
second meaning: a ballet skirt hangs around a dancer's waist

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the South African archbishop's surname and the stiff short skirt ballerinas wear.

clue.text: See 18
In vain, Rushdie contains flood

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer inside them, running across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of vain and the start of Rushdie

explanation.surface: Salman Rushdie, in hiding from the fatwa, futilely holds back a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' says the letters sit inside 'vain, Rushdie'; the opening 'In' is a link, not part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flowing in, as of water, so it is a flood or surge.

clue.text: Where parliament meets bitter force constraining unruly brats

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the jumbled piece in, confining it

parts.note: sour means bitter
G is the physics abbreviation for gravitational force

indicators.note: badly behaved, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh disciplinary regime keeps rowdy children in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter force' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces; 'unruly' gives TRASB, and 'constraining' wraps the pieces round it, just after their opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Parliament holds its plenary sessions in this city in Alsace, France.

clue.text: PM no longer with us — paradise!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Anthony ..., Prime Minister 1955-57, died in 1977
second meaning: the Garden of ..., the biblical paradise

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the surname of the late Suez-era premier and the biblical garden of perfect bliss.
